name: HDB Financial Services Ltd
title: HDB Financial Services Ltd - 544429 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: HDB Financial Q4 FY26 shows credit-cost and Stage 3 improvement (GNPA 2.44% vs 2.81%) and record disbursements of ₹19,922 crore, but book growth of 3.4% QoQ and no supply-side discipline story; a growth-recovery read, not a capital-cycle trigger.

triggers.label: Q4 disbursements ₹19,922 cr, highest ever
triggers.quote: Disbursements for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, was ₹19,922 crores, up 11.2% sequentially – an all-time high

triggers.label: Gross Stage 3 2.44% vs 2.81%
triggers.quote: Gross Stage 3 as at March 31, 2026, was 2.44% as against 2.81% as at March 31, 2025.

triggers.label: NIM 8.23% vs 8.09% QoQ
triggers.quote: Net interest margin for Q4 FY26 was 8.23% vs 8.09% in Q3 FY26

we wished for it to moderate in the range of 2.3% plus/minus
an 8 %+ is a non -negotiable the way we treat it internally today
I think we will range around 3.7%

summary.headline: HDB Financial Q4 FY26: PAT rose 16.6% QoQ to ₹751 crore, NIM expanded to 8.23% and Gross Stage 3 fell to 2.44%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential improvement on profitability, margins and asset quality. Disbursements hit a record ₹19,922 crore (up 11.2% QoQ), but gross loan book growth was only 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY. NIM rose 16 bps QoQ to 8.23%, helped by lower borrowing costs, while yield dipped 7-8 bps on product mix. Management said March went well and it has not yet seen level 2/3 impact from the West Asia conflict, which it flagged as a key monitorable.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.09% in Q3 FY26, 7.55% in Q4 FY25
vs 41.6% in Q3 FY26, 42.9% in Q4 FY25
vs 2.81% at Dec 31, 2025 and at Mar 31, 2025 per Q&A

segments.name: Enterprise lending
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements grew ~27.9% QoQ and ~15.4% YoY. LAP+EBL book grew 3.8% QoQ on ~36% disbursement growth. Enterprise lending Stage 3 fell to 1.58% from 1.82% in Q3 and 1.79% a year ago.

segments.name: Asset finance (CV/CE)
segments.commentary: Book showed moderate growth in Q4. Gross Stage 3 moved 3.14% (Q4 FY25) to 4.3% (Q3 FY26) to 3.79% (Q4 FY26). FY26 disbursements declined ~3% per analyst; management is pushing used vehicles, with a 50:50 new/used target over four years.

segments.name: Consumer finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 5.3% QoQ and 19.4% YoY, led by consumer durables then auto loans. Stage 3 rose to 2.44% from 2.26% a year ago, but improved from Q3.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book doubled in FY26; disbursements grew 58.7% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth target: nominal GDP + 6-7% CAGR, with the three-year agenda; management declined to give specific numbers.
Credit cost to moderate to around 2.3% (+/- ) and be sustainable at that level over the medium term.
NIM to be maintained at 8% or above, described as non-negotiable in 2/3/5-year plans; Q4 was 8.23%.
FY27 opex-to-gross loan book expected around 3.7% (FY26 was ~3.8%); cost-to-income guided to a similar range.
Cost of borrowings expected to hold for at least the current quarter; the CP mix is low and bank loans are below 50% of borrowings.
Expects Q1 to be seasonally slower; comparisons should be made Q1 vs Q1, not Q1 vs Q4. Ambition is YoY disbursement growth of 18-20%, described as hopeful, not committed.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 1,730 across 1,161 towns and cities; 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, with consolidation into larger formats (600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft).
Management said no square footage has been reduced in the last three quarters as a listed company.
DIY digital sourcing grew ~2.2x in FY26; management expects it to grow further (2x to 5x cited).
App downloads at 1.41 crore; 4.76 lakh daily active users.
Five large AI-powered initiatives underway; bot-based collections nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4, improving early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps.
demand_pricing: Management says all product yields were held in Q4; the 7-8 bps yield decline was from product mix, with unsecured disbursement growth lagging. Yield should return with unsecured growth, staying within the 14%+ range.
Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursements were ₹15,599 crore, ₹17,917 crore and ₹19,922 crore respectively.
Secured share of gross loans is 74%, up from the 72% level management has held historically.
Borrowing costs have risen across the market over the past month, per management; the company has no low-cost borrowings left to reset after the last tranche in Oct-Nov 2025.
Average exposure per customer is ~₹1.66 lakh; the retail book is 100% of the portfolio.
AUM mix is 38:38:24 (enterprise lending : asset finance : consumer finance), expected to move to roughly 38:37:25 in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in March and early April on the West Asia conflict, supply chains and CV operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March went well and is reflected in the results; no level 2/3 impact seen so far. It remains a key monitorable, with a 15-20 day watch period.

qa_highlights.question: Were contingency or buffer provisions considered for MSME/SME stress?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific level 2/3 impact seen yet. Management said LAP and MSME challenges were resolved by the March quarter and the focus is now growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35 bps QoQ fall in cost of funds and can it be sustained given market rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it held lending rates and worked on borrowing strategies; no low-cost borrowings remain to reset. Cost of funds should hold for the current quarter, though market rates have risen.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 PCR rise by 30 bps, and why did enterprise lending PCR fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is refreshed quarterly on an automated ECL basis (fully automated this quarter) using PD, LGD and product mix. Management said there is no one-time item.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset finance Stage 3 recover so quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery has been K-shaped: accounts challenged in Q1 recovered slowly, while newer slippages are recovering faster. Management pushed recoveries and flow-forward reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM be sustained at 8%+ and what about branch additions?
qa_highlights.answer: 8%+ NIM is non-negotiable in internal plans; Q4 was 8.23%. Branch count will change by 20-30 sites through consolidation and upsizing, with digital channels driving growth.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict, supply chain disruption and El Nino impact on CV and MSME repayments; management says it is too early to call second- and third-order effects.
Rising market borrowing costs (CP mix low, bank loans below 50%), which could pressure the 8%+ NIM.
Disbursement-to-book conversion: book growth of 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY is still below the nominal GDP + 6-7% aspiration.
Asset finance Stage 3 at 3.79% and consumer finance Stage 3 at 2.44%; sustainability of the recovery and the used-vehicle push.
Write-off quantum for FY26 and Q4 was not disclosed on the call; to be provided offline.
Yield dilution from product mix until unsecured business loans regain growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on growth and NIM discipline. Cautious and evasive on the West Asia conflict, borrowing-cost outlook and forward growth numbers, which were framed as hopes rather than targets.
key_quotes: Gross NPA, which we also report as Gross Stage 3 – we don't report two different numbers – reduced to 2.44% as at March 31, 2026 vs 2.81% as at December 31, 2025.
But an 8 %+ is a non-negotiable the way we treat it internally today.
So, we haven't seen any major disruption is the way I would put it.
I would like to think at least for the current quarter we're good, right?

adds.what: 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, with consolidation into larger formats (600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft)

growth.why: Management targets nominal GDP + 6-7% medium-term AUM growth and YoY disbursement growth of 18-20% (hopeful, not committed), backed by record Q4 disbursements of ₹19,922 cr and a 20-30 branch addition/relocation plan, but no specific numbers were given for the medium-term target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM rose to 8.23% in Q4 from 8.09% in Q3 and cost-to-income in lending fell to 39.5% from 41.6%, with opex/gross loan book guided to ~3.7% vs ~3.8% in FY26 and credit cost moderating toward ~2.3% from 2.35%; however, cost of borrowings is rising market-wide and management only guarantees cost of funds for the current quarter, so NIM is guided to hold at 8%+ rather than expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch count is 1,730 and 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, mainly via consolidation into larger 600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft formats, but net branch additions are not quantified and the change is largely format-driven rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward, compare Q1 vs Q1
rows.why: Q4 disbursements hit a record ₹19,922 crore (+11.2% QoQ) and the book grew 10.9% YoY to ₹1,18,493 crore, with management targeting 18-20% YoY disbursement growth as a hope rather than a commitment, while Q1 is guided to be seasonally slower.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all guidance (NIM 8%+, credit cost ~2.3%, opex ~3.7%) and described the 18-20% disbursement ambition as hopeful, not committed, with the book still well below the nominal GDP + 6-7% aspiration at 10.9% YoY growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia conflict and El Nino risks to CV and MSME repayments are unquantified (management is watching a 15-20 day window), and rising market borrowing costs could pressure the 8%+ NIM given no low-cost borrowings remain to reset after Oct-Nov 2025.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Used-vehicle push in asset finance targeting a 50:50 new/used mix over four years and DIY digital sourcing growing ~2.2x in FY26 (expected 2x to 5x) are ongoing initiatives, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Record disbursement momentum into Q1 FY27
rows.why: Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursements rose from ₹15,599 cr to ₹17,917 cr to ₹19,922 cr, but management guides Q1 to be seasonally slower and the 18-20% YoY ambition is hopeful rather than committed.

rows.label: Asset quality recovery sustainability
rows.why: Gross Stage 3 fell to 2.44% from 2.81% in Q3 and the enterprise Stage 3 to 1.58%, but asset finance Stage 3 is still 3.79% and recovery is K-shaped, so the improvement depends on continued collections and the West Asia/El Nino outcome.

rows.label: AI-driven collections efficiency
rows.why: Bot-based nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4 and improved early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps, with five large AI initiatives underway.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM discipline (8%+ non-negotiable), asset quality (Stage 3 down to 2.44%) and record disbursements, but cautious on the West Asia conflict, rising borrowing costs and forward growth, framing the 18-20% disbursement target as hope; analysts pushed on cost of funds sustain
